summary.text: 旁 commonly means “side,” “beside,” or “near.” The traditional analysis treats 方 as a sound component, but leaves the upper element unexplained; its identity and contribution remain unsettled.

formation.text: The traditional dictionary describes 旁 as phonosemantic: 方 supplies a sound cue, while the explanation of the upper part is marked as missing. Early forms have also been analyzed as 方 combined with an unidentified element, possibly 凡, but that identification and any semantic role remain uncertain.

components.text: 方 is identified as the sound element in the traditional analysis. In the supplied Baxter–Sagart entries, 方 *paŋ and 旁 *[b]ˤaŋ share the rhyme but differ in initial notation. The sound-series identification is documented, while the precise historical comparison is limited by the available evidence.

sound_limitation.text: The historical dictionary identifies 方 as a sound element, and the supplied forms are compatible in rhyme. The available comparison does not independently establish the exact historical sound relationship.

sound.text: These Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese forms share the rhyme but differ in initial notation; 方 has multiple listed lexical entries.
The Mandarin readings share the final -ang but have different initials; this modern comparison does not establish their ancient relationship.

history.text: Historical dictionary records list 𣃟 and 𣃙 as ancient-script forms and 雱 as a Zhou-script form. A Chu silk-script form is also identified, but its modern redraw was not visually inspected. These records do not establish a stroke-by-stroke sequence or settle the upper element’s identity.

A paleographic reference reports early inscription uses in place, polity, and personal names, and a Spring-and-Autumn directional use read as 方. Those reported uses do not show that the common meaning “side” was already present.

The Shuowen account gives the gloss 溥 and marks the explanation of an element as 闕. The note’s authorship and referent are disputed; the available abstract reports one view that it arose through graphic change, without exposing the full paleographic argument.

uncertainties.text: The upper element’s identity and meaning remain unresolved. A reduced 凡 has been proposed, alongside other identifications, but the available evidence does not establish its original form or contribution.
The first use of 旁 meaning “side” or “near” is not dated here. No semantic development from 溥, interpreted as “broad” or “abundant,” to “side” is established.

senses.text: 旁 is used with the meanings “side,” “beside,” and “near.” The first attested use of these meanings is not dated in the available evidence.
The traditional dictionary glosses 旁 as 溥; later commentary interprets this as “broad” or “abundant.” This lexicographic account does not establish the graph’s original meaning.

limitations.text: No dated semantic link is established between the traditional gloss 溥 (“broad” or “abundant”) and the common meanings “side” or “near.” The reported early name and directional uses do not establish that link either.
